clue.text: Demanding type at home with nurse

parts.note: at home means in, as in 'she is in tonight'
a sister is a senior nurse in British hospitals

explanation.surface: A pushy person who lives with a nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who insists on things is a demanding sort of person, a stickler who will not let a point go.

clue.text: One writing about wine buys from abroad

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: about means the writing goes around the wine

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A writer on wine purchases bottles from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One writing' looks like the subject of the sentence but gives I + MS.
explanation.definitionFit: A country or merchant that brings in goods from overseas is purchasing them from foreign sellers.

clue.text: Youth leader in school adding twice as much

indicators.note: leader in means the first letter of the word school

parts.note: adding twice as much again makes something three times as big

explanation.surface: A youth club head at a school doubling the numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Youth leader' reads as one phrase; split it: 'Youth' is the definition, 'leader in school' is S.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripling is a lad, a young man not yet fully grown.

clue.text: Poles holding male social gathering in pub

indicators.note: holding means the poles go around the other pieces

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
he is the male pronoun
a bee is a gathering for work and company, as in a sewing bee

explanation.surface: People from Poland hosting a men's get-together in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests people from Poland; it is the two compass poles. A shebeen is an unlicensed Irish or Scottish drinking den.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an illicit drinking house, chiefly Irish, Scottish or South African.

clue.text: Taken out of context, remedy is Draconian

indicators.note: Taken out of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cure that sounds harsh when quoted out of context.
explanation.definitionFit: Draconian means harsh beyond measure, like the severe laws of Draco of Athens.

clue.text: Beef high on the menu, perhaps

explanation.surface: Beef featuring prominently on a restaurant menu.
explanation.walkthrough: Game birds are traditionally hung until 'high' (gamey) before cooking, so the game bird may be high on the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef is to complain, a sense shared by the moorland game bird's name; that bird is hung until gamey before it is eaten.

clue.text: Old bomber in raid Green, organized

indicators.note: organized means the letters of the two words are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A bomber in a planned raid on a village green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old bomber' suggests a wartime aircraft; it is a soldier who once threw grenades.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenadiers were originally soldiers who threw hand grenades, an early kind of bomb.

clue.text: Committing offence, having gone overboard?

explanation.surface: Someone who broke the rules after going too far.
explanation.walkthrough: In football a player beyond the last defender commits an offside offence; going over the side of a boat puts one literally 'off side'.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, being in an illegal position ahead of the ball; read literally, off the side of a ship.

clue.text: Hide in quarters on island

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the quarters sit above the island

parts.note: S and E are quarters, or points, of the compass
Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: Lie low in lodgings on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' suggests lodgings to hide in, but means compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to conceal it, stashing it away out of sight.

clue.text: Centre page spread showing profit

indicators.note: spread means the letters of the two words are scattered and laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A magazine's middle pages showing how much a firm made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre page spread' reads as a magazine feature, but 'spread' is the anagram signal on CENTRE PAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Profit is often expressed as a cut or share, as in taking a percentage of the takings.

clue.text: Brave fiancée's odd constituents

indicators.note: the odd constituents are the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the word fiancée

explanation.surface: A bold bride-to-be's peculiar supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' looks like an adjective describing the fiancée but is a verb, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To brave something is to confront it boldly, meeting it head-on.

clue.text: Typical traveller

explanation.surface: An ordinary commercial traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'commercial traveller' is a travelling salesman, a sales rep.
explanation.definitionFit: Typical means standing as an example of a class; a commercial traveller is a salesman sent out on behalf of a firm.

clue.text: Since Reformation, church's branch of knowledge

indicators.note: a re-formation of the word since means its letters are formed again in a new order

parts.note: CE is short for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Since the Reformation, the church has had its own field of learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformation' suggests the 16th-century religious upheaval, which fits 'church', but it reshapes SINCE into SCIEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A science is a systematic field of study, physics or biology for example.

clue.text: Agreement doctor can change

indicators.note: change means the letters of doctor and can are rearranged

explanation.surface: A deal that a GP might be able to alter.
explanation.definitionFit: A concordat is a formal pact, especially one between a state and the Vatican.

clue.text: Order to soldiers to shoot brigade members

explanation.surface: An officer's command to open fire, given to members of a brigade.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits as 'Fire, men!', a command to troops; 'brigade' suggests the army but means the fire brigade.
explanation.definitionFit: A shouted command telling troops to shoot; those who belong to a fire-fighting service.

clue.text: Admirer of new navy one found in humble surroundings

indicators.note: found in means the navy and the one sit within the word for humble
surroundings says the word for humble forms the walls around the other pieces

parts.note: humble means modest
RN is the Royal Navy
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A fan of novelty, a sailor living in poor conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new navy' tempts a reading about a modern fleet; 'new' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion of contemporary styles and ideas in preference to tradition.

clue.text: Fancy fruit imported, we hear

parts.note: a fig is a soft sweet fruit

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken for its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: to import is an old sense of to signify, so imported means meant

explanation.surface: Exotic fruit brought in from abroad, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy fruit imported' reads as exotic produce, but 'Fancy' is the noun definition and 'imported' means signified.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy in the sense of something imagined, an invention of the mind rather than reality.

clue.text: Naughty child's taken-over changed for better

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

indicators.note: taken, in the sense of taken apart, means the letters of over are reordered

explanation.surface: A naughty child has seized control, and things got better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken over' looks like one phrase meaning seized; 'taken' scrambles OVER into ROVE. The definition is loose: it means to change for the better.
explanation.definitionFit: To improve is to make or become better, a change of quality upward.

clue.text: Easy author

parts.note: Easy is not an adjective but the title hero of the 1836 novel Mr Midshipman Easy, so this is the writer of that book

explanation.surface: A writer who is undemanding to read.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Frederick Marryat wrote the naval novel Mr Midshipman Easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Frederick Marryat was the Victorian naval novelist behind Mr Midshipman Easy.

clue.text: Licence specially granted by city sometimes

explanation.surface: A permit that a city grants as a special favour.
explanation.walkthrough: A city may confer its 'freedom' on a distinguished person as an honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Licence as liberty to act as one pleases; the civic honour a city confers on notable citizens.

clue.text: Thrill for loving and giving boy?

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme, Friday's child is loving and giving, so this is FRI'S, Friday's
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: An excitement for a loving and generous lad.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'Monday's child is fair of face' gives each weekday's child a trait; Friday's is 'loving and giving'.
explanation.definitionFit: A frisson is a sudden shiver of excitement.

clue.text: Call for defence to foil attack

definitions.text: Call for defence to foil attack

parts.words: Call for defence to foil attack
parts.note: foil is the fencing sword, and the call is the French warning a fencer gives to be ready to parry

explanation.surface: A cry to rally defenders and thwart an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foil' looks like a verb meaning thwart; it is the fencing weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The French call telling fencers to take guard before a bout.

clue.text: Plant in my control

indicators.note: in means the plant sits inside the word my

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like flowering plant

explanation.surface: A plant under my command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' may suggest a factory; it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastery is command or domination over something.

clue.text: By creating star, transformed ballet etc

parts.note: creating, as in creating a scene, means performing

indicators.note: transformed means the word star is changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Ballet and the like turned someone into a star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creating star' reads as making someone famous; 'creating' is PERFORMING and 'transformed' rearranges STAR into ARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballet is one of the stage disciplines, alongside drama, music and opera.

clue.text: Quality of wine, not spirit

explanation.surface: A wine's character, as opposed to spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' looks like strong drink, beside wine, but means the soul as opposed to the flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: Fullness of flavour and texture in a wine; the physical frame as opposed to the soul.

clue.text: Little girl's first shot hurt

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name (Diana), so a little girl's gives DI'S
in tennis the service is the first shot of each point

explanation.surface: A young girl's opening shot that injured someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hurt' looks like a verb but is a noun here, meaning harm.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurt is an injury or wrong done to someone, an ill turn.

clue.text: Go away, it appears, after defeat

indicators.note: after means the word it comes after the synonym for defeat

parts.note: to beat is to defeat

explanation.surface: Get lost, as it seems after a loss.
explanation.definitionFit: A slangy command telling someone to leave, like 'clear off'.

clue.text: Descent for those in tree

parts.note: the tree is a family tree, and the descent is lineage, not a climb down from the branches

explanation.surface: How the creatures in a tree come down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Descent' and 'tree' paint climbing down from the branches; the tree is genealogical.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage from forebears is what a family chart records.
